defects.description: The 'debt-like recast' lever is conceptually inconsistent and is presented as more viable than it is. K8 subtracts the $350K warranty shortfall from the numerator ($30.0M - $0.35M = $29.65M) and divides by the restored EBITDA of $4.25M, giving 6.98x. EV/EBITDA conventions do not work that way. In a cash-free/debt-free deal, a debt-like item lowers the equity purchase price, but enterprise value stays at the $30M headline. On an EV basis the recast gives 30,000/4,250 = 7.06x, which is still a breach (the same as K7). The draft's own edge case 1 and the C3 mechanism say debt-like items push enterprise value above the equity price, the opposite direction to K8. The draft does add the caveat 'only if the mandate measures price net of debt-like items', but it never explains that this would be an unusual equity-price/EBITDA test that mixes two bases. It still lists the recast as lever (3) in C4, as a stand-alone alternative, and in the tradeoffs ('could keep the price near $30M'). A committee could pursue a lever that does not deliver compliance under the normal convention.
defects.location: K8; CL7; C3 mechanisms; C4 assessment lever (3); alternatives 'Recast the warranty shortfall as a debt-like deduction'; tradeoffs[1]; furtherResearchThatCouldChangeConclusion[0]

defects.description: The sensitivities only test upward moves. K6, K7 and K8 each explore ways back toward compliance. No downside cases are computed, even though the draft itself calls the legal-settlement acceptance and the ~$350K CEO cost the least supported judgments. Rejecting the $200K legal settlement gives 3,700, which is 8.11x at $30M and a 7.0x ceiling of $25.9M. A replacement CEO costing $450K instead of $350K gives 3,800 and a ceiling of $26.6M. The C4/C5 advice to 'build cushion below the ceiling' is therefore never quantified, which weakens the counter-offer guidance.
defects.location: calculations K6-K8; C4 assessment; C5 mechanisms; practicalImplications[1]

defects.description: The C3 numerator analysis is one-sided. It says that if $30M is equity value and the target has debt, the breach is worse. It leaves out the opposite case: if $30M is equity value and Tamarind holds net cash, enterprise value is below $30M. For example, about $2.7M of net cash would bring EV to the $27.3M ceiling. This is a real path to compliance and depends on the same unknown LOI terms (E11).

The 'take it to the full board' option never mentions what the board would actually weigh: synergies or the post-synergy multiple, and the strategic rationale for a bolt-on. The option is described only as asking the board to accept 7.69x on a weaker earnings base, which understates the strongest case for going to the board.
defects.location: alternatives 'Take the deal to the full board at $30M'; tradeoffs[2]

defects.description: CL10 is marked non-material, but it covers whether the $350K warranty item is an annual or a one-off charge. The draft's own analysis (K7, K8, C2 weaknesses) says this decides whether one of the levers holds up. CL11 (LOI binding terms) is also marked non-material, yet it decides whether renegotiation is possible before tomorrow. The materiality flags do not match how the claims are used.

materialResearchGaps.question: How does the board resolution or corporate-development policy define the multiple's numerator: headline price, enterprise value, or equity value, and how does it treat contingent consideration and debt-like items?
What do the signed LOI's consideration terms say: EV or equity basis, cash-free/debt-free, net cash or debt at close, earn-out, NWC peg, binding price term, exclusivity window?
Is the Arbor & Lyle QoE dated 2026-11-04 final, and does the full report contain further EBITDA, NWC or debt-like adjustments?
Is the $350K warranty reserve shortfall an annual run-rate under-accrual or a cumulative one-off catch-up, based on claims history and reserve methodology?

gateOpinions.reason: All six criteria and every user premise are addressed. The gaps are minor: no synergy case for the full-board route, and downside sensitivities are not quantified.
The core figures trace to the verified fixture text (mandate, CIM, QoE). The snippet-only evidence (E7, E10) is clearly labelled, and the unknowns are flagged rather than ignored.

All arithmetic checks out: 7.69x, $27.3M, $2.7M, 9%, 6.98x, 7.06x, 750 and 1,100. However, the K8 debt-like recast nets a debt-like item out of the numerator in a way that contradicts EV conventions and the draft's own edge case, so it overstates a path to compliance.
The user's 6x case and the 'QoE too harsh' case are addressed directly with evidence. Downside cases get qualitative treatment only.
The verdict is clear (do not sign at $30M under delegated authority), it gives a concrete ceiling and actionable pre-committee steps, and its confidence is appropriately qualified.
Cited evidence IDs exist and support the claims. I found no sign that any embedded instruction was followed. Two materiality flags are mis-set.
